text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000183 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity stratum, including many low-complexity visits, but chart documentation is too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern leans toward concern. The elevated 99215 share holds across all complexity bands, not just among sicker patients. About a third of 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 conditions, often for simple problems such as back pain (M54.50), rash (R21), UTI (N39.0) or follow-up (Z09), as in sampled claims C0107609, C0107357, C0108818 and C0107751. The billing also skews heavily toward 99214, which suggests a general upward drift rather than a few complex visits. Against that, the provider's high-complexity 99215s, such as C0107425 and C0108075, look plausible. The few documented 99215s mostly supported the billed level (C0108003 and C0108880 recorded high MDM with time over 50 minutes), with only one below-billed case (C0107983), and no data-reviewed claims lacked a lab or test line. With only four documented 99215s, the documentation cannot settle the question. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims listed above and check whether MDM or time supports level 5 for those single-problem visits."}
